intentAndPurpose.intent: Compact interactive label for filtering, tagging, or selecting values.

props.name: attention
props.description: Emphasis level — high (filled when selected), medium (tinted when selected), low (outlined). Default: 'high'.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: QA / automation hook on the root toggle button

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Default selected state (uncontrolled). Defaults to true.

props.name: end
props.description: Content to render after the label (Icon, Avatar, CounterBadge, IndicatorBadge)

props.name: selected
props.description: Selected state (controlled). Maps to Toggle pressed.

props.name: start
props.description: Content to render before the label (Icon, Avatar, CounterBadge, IndicatorBadge)

interactionBehavior.summary: Chip is a Base UI Toggle, so every click flips a selected state — and it starts SELECTED unless you pass `defaultSelected={false}` or a controlled `selected`. Selection, not attention, is what drives the colour: `attention` only decides how the selected state looks (filled / tinted / outlined). The counter-intuitive part is the unselected chrome — its stroke and its hover/pressed tints come from the nearest `<Surface>` role via `data-unselected-appearance`, NOT from the chip's own `appearance` prop, and they fall back to Neutral on a bare page. Chip has no press-scale at all: feedback is entirely fill, stroke, and text colour.
hover: Every hover rule is wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck hover fill behind.

UNSELECTED (any attention level) picks up the same tint: `--{ParentSurfaceRole}-Hover`, resolved through `data-unselected-appearance` — so an `appearance="negative"` chip that is not selected still hovers Neutral on a plain page, and inherits the surrounding Surface's role inside a tinted one.
SELECTED at `attention="high"` steps the fill and the border to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover`; at `medium` the fill steps to `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`.
SELECTED at `attention="low"` is the odd one: its rest state is transparent with an accent hairline, so hover ADDS a fill of `--{Role}-Subtle` rather than deepening an existing one.
Label and icon colours never change on hover — only background, and (for selected high) the border.
A chip whose role carries a metallic material keeps `--{Role}-Material-Fill` on hover, because swapping a flat colour in over a gradient reads as a glitch.
press: Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a touch tap gets the same immediate fill feedback a mouse press does.
UNSELECTED presses to `--{ParentSurfaceRole}-Pressed` — again the Surface-derived role, not the chip's `appearance`.
SELECTED presses to `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` (high, fill + border) or `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` (medium); selected low goes to `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`, one step past its hover fill.
The chip does NOT scale, translate, or move on press — there is no `transform` anywhere in Chip's CSS, unlike Button (scales down) and IconButton (scales up).
focus: Keyboard focus draws the standard two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer ring at `calc(--Stroke-XL + --Focus-Outline-Width)` in `--Focus-Outline`, so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
The ring follows the pill radius (`--Chip-borderRadius`, default `--Shape-Pill`), and ornament radii if the brand sets them.
`:focus` alone only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click selects the chip without painting a halo.
The halo is a `box-shadow`, and the chip's own edge is a real `border`, so focusing never disturbs the outline of a `medium` chip.
keyboard: Base UI Toggle renders a native `<button aria-pressed>`, so `Enter` and `Space` both toggle selection — both paths are covered by tests.

Inside a `ChipGroup` the chips become a Base UI ToggleGroup composite: arrow keys rove focus between chips (one tab stop for the whole group), `loopFocus` defaults to true so focus wraps, and `orientation` defaults to horizontal.

`ChipGroup`'s `required` and `maxSelections` constraints are enforced in the group's change handler, so a keystroke that would drop below the minimum or exceed the maximum is simply ignored — the chip does not visibly toggle.
A disabled chip is natively `disabled`, so it is out of the tab order and cannot hold roving focus.
selected: Selected maps to Base UI Toggle's `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and matched in CSS with `[data-pressed]`.
It defaults to TRUE in uncontrolled mode (`defaultSelected ?? true`) — a bare `<Chip>Filter</Chip>` renders already selected. Pass `defaultSelected={false}` for a filter row that starts empty.

`appearance` colours the SELECTED look only: high → `--{Role}-Bold` fill with `--{Role}-Bold-High` text; medium → `--{Role}-Subtle` fill, `--{Role}-High` text and the border goes transparent; low → transparent fill with a `--{Role}-Tinted` hairline. `appearance="auto"` (the default) resolves to `secondary`, or to the parent Surface's role.

Unselected is deliberately neutral chrome: high → `--{ParentSurfaceRole}-Minimal` fill, medium → transparent plus a `--{ParentSurfaceRole}-Stroke-Medium` hairline, low → fully transparent; all three keep `--Text-High` labels.
A selected high/medium chip publishes `data-surface="bold"` / `"subtle"` onto its `start` and `end` slot wrappers, so an Avatar inside re-resolves as a real nested surface on top of the chip fill.

`CounterBadge` and `IndicatorBadge` children are auto-wrapped in a `data-context-boundary` span so they keep their own semantic colour instead of inheriting the chip's surface — red stays red on a selected chip.
Selecting a high-attention chip also switches slot icons from `--{Role}-Tinted` to `--{Role}-Bold-Tinted`.
disabled: `disabled` on the chip emits `data-disabled`, which dims it to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed` plus `pointer-events: none`. Setting `disabled` on the `ChipGroup` instead propagates through Base UI's group context and natively disables each toggle.

Because the underlying button is natively `disabled` AND has `pointer-events: none`, the `not-allowed` cursor is not observable — the pointer shows the parent's cursor. Known, accepted system-wide gap (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
Every hover and pressed rule is qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`, so a disabled chip is visually inert in both selected and unselected states.
The disabled chip keeps whatever selected styling it had — disabling does not clear or grey out the selection, it only dims it.
touch: On touch-only devices the hover fills never apply; the pressed fill is the entire visual response to a tap, since there is no press-scale.
The whole chip is the hit target — label, `start`, and `end` slots are all inside the toggle button, and slot content is not separately clickable.
Chip heights and paddings come from the layout matrix per size and slot combination, so the touch target grows with `size="l"` rather than with a CSS min-height.
